title: The debate at Achal
hookLine: at Achal Batala the yogis test Nanak with miracles; he says his only miracle is the true Name (Bhai Gurdas, Var 1)

lines: A FAIR AT ACHAL, ON SHIVRATRI.
THE YOGIS DON'T TAKE IT WELL.
cards: A fair is a noisy place: stalls, crowds, music, smoke from cooking fires, people who've walked all day to be there.
Bhai Gurdas tells of one at Achal, near Batala, for Shivratri, a festival of Shiva, with yogis gathered there. Baba Nanak came, and the whole crowd turned to see him.
The yogis did not take it well, and Bhai Gurdas tells what followed without softening it. Today: Achal.

teach.b: Bhai Gurdas says the yogis burned with jealousy when they saw it. The debate starts sharp. A yogi named Bhangar Nath goes after the very thing you heard about yesterday.

You were a wanderer, he says, and now you've gone back to a householder's life. Isn't that spoiling the milk? Nanak's answer turns it around: you left home behind, and yet you go begging at householders' doors.
Then the yogis try a different kind of argument. Bhai Gurdas describes them showing off their powers, taking strange shapes, doing marvels, and then turning to Nanak. Show us something, they say.
The whole world has seen what you can do.
Show us a miracle too. Here is the line at the center of today.

teach.h: NO MIRACLE BUT THE TRUE NAME.
teach.b: Nanak answers that apart from the true Name, he has no other miracle. In the same exchange he says there's no other support for him but the Guru's company and the Guru's word.
Notice what he's refusing: to make holiness a contest of who can astonish whom.

A miracle performed to win an argument is a show, and a show is about the performer. The Name points away from the performer, toward the One. Bhai Gurdas sets that one plain sentence against all the yogis' marvels.

how: Sikhs remember Guru Nanak's answer at Achal, as Bhai Gurdas tells it, as a teaching that the Name, not wonder-working, is the heart of the path.

o: a cave where yogis kept a fire burning for years
a river crossing where Nanak healed a sick child
the fair where Nanak said the Name was his only miracle

games.q: who said what — tap the pairs.
p: no miracle but the true Name

s: at Achal, Nanak beats the yogis with a bigger miracle
he says that apart from the true Name, he has no miracle.
the yogis were jealous because the crowd went to Nanak
Bhangar Nath criticized Nanak for becoming a householder
and Nanak answered that the yogis beg at householders' doors.

games.q: you're at a crowded fair. rival holy men have just shown off their powers, and now they turn to you: show us a miracle. what do you do?
o: outdo them, so the crowd knows who's greater.
say the true Name is your only miracle.
games.why: in Bhai Gurdas's telling, Nanak says that apart from the true Name he has no other miracle, and no support but the Guru's company and word.

practice: Picture a moment coming today when you could be impressive, mentioning the thing you did, topping someone's story with a bigger one, being the cleverest voice in the room, and then picture letting it pass: not hiding anything, just not performing.
Notice how the urge feels in your body and let it settle; if you pray, you can say the Name quietly in the place where the show would have been.

wordCard.voice: Achal, the fair near Batala where yogis demanded a miracle, and Nanak said that apart from the true Name, he had none.

carryVoice: Your line: the only miracle. One plain sentence, set against all the marvels. Until tomorrow.
